state.user_request_16_nov: Write a debugging model for the backend and the front end, so any issue faced can be debugged. When the application is finished we need a log of whatever is being run, as it is a broadcast. Everything being logged is a good thing, so nothing is randomly flagged. Jev and Laya agree design and acceptance and review what is built.
facts: Processes: render engine worker and host, Editor (Tauri shell, TypeScript front end, editor service), Playout (Tauri shell, JavaScript front end), editor MCP and playout MCP servers. Program output is a 50 fps clock; nothing may stall it (invariant 14).

gx-telemetry (rows 0.5, 2.10 done) has typed audit and operations events, a Redacted type so credentials never reach a log line, and init() that writes formatted text to stdout. No product depends on it; the engine prints plain eprintln lines; the front ends log nothing; there is no log file anywhere.

platform::log_root() names the per-user log directory. Row 12.11 (as-run record, first-release scope, pending, its dependencies done) asks every accepted or refused Cue, Take, Update, Continue, Out and Clear to write one record to a JSON Lines audit sink with sequence, intent id, operator identity and scope, page, revision, hash, target, result and the engine-committed frame, and replaying a fixture show's records to match the engine's committed events.

Control-plane intents carry an id; the Editor front end calls the shell through one execute command and a few read commands; Playout through cmd_cue, cmd_take, cmd_clear, cmd_phase, cmd_configure_output.
state.proposal: One event schema in gx-telemetry: JSON Lines with UTC time, monotonic time, per-process sequence, process, pid, level, event name, correlation id, typed sanitised fields, engine epoch and frame where known. Each process writes its own file under log_root, through a bounded queue drained by a writer thread so the frame path never waits on disk; on overflow the count of lost events is itself written as a record, never a silent gap. Every state change, command, refusal, connection, publish and frame-timing anomaly is logged at info; debug and trace are opt-in. Front ends forward errors, unhandled rejections and every shell call (start, end, refusal, duration) through one log command with a correlation id that follows the action into the engine. The as-run log is separate: append-only, flushed and synced per record, hash-chained so a missing or edited line is detectable, not rotated during a show. Operational logs rotate by size and keep 30 days. One command makes a sanitised diagnostic bundle.

criteria.json_lines: Structured JSON Lines, one event per line, stable field names.

criteria.per_process_files_one_schema: Each process writes its own file under log_root with the shared schema; a correlation id joins them.
criteria.central_collector: Every process sends events to one collector process that writes them.
criteria.stdout_only: Stdout only; the launcher captures it.

overflow.instructions: What happens when logging cannot keep up?

criteria.bounded_queue_log_the_loss: Bounded queue; the frame path never waits; lost events are counted and the count is written as a record.
criteria.block_until_written: Wait until each event is written.

as_run.instructions: How should the broadcast as-run log be kept?

criteria.separate_durable_hash_chained: A separate append-only file, synced per record and hash-chained, never dropped: the record of what went to air.
criteria.same_stream: The same stream and queue as operational logs.

frontend.instructions: How should the front ends log?

criteria.forward_through_shell: Errors, unhandled rejections and every shell call go through one log command into the shell's file, with the action's correlation id.

criteria.all_state_changes_info: Every command, refusal, state change and anomaly at info; debug and trace opt-in.

criteria.rotate_30_days_as_run_kept: Operational logs rotate by size and are kept 30 days; the as-run log is never rotated during a show and is kept until archived.

criteria.one_command_bundle: One command collects the recent logs of every process, versions, capability and sanitised configuration.
criteria.manual: The user finds and sends files by hand.

needs_user.instructions: Must the user approve this design before implementation?

criteria.true: Yes, product choices are made the user's request does not cover.
criteria.false: No, it follows from the user's request, rows 2.10 and 12.11 and the invariants.
